tools.name: Welcome to DDD
tools.note: The gentlest front door in the whole ddd-crew set. Send someone here before anything with a canvas on it.

tools.name: DDD Starter Modelling Process
tools.note: The one that turns reading into doing: an order to work in when you have no idea where to start. Pairs with Maxime Sanglan-Charlier's talk explaining it.

tools.name: DDD Familiarity Assessment
tools.note: Useful for finding out what a team already knows before you teach them things they do not need.

tools.name: Free DDD learning resources
tools.note: The comprehensive free list, which is exactly why we should not build our own. We curate a path; this is the library at the end of it.

tools.name: AI DDD prompts & rules
tools.note: DDD prompts and rules for a coding assistant. Not licensed for republishing, so we link out.

tools.name: Context Mapping
tools.note: The patterns for how contexts relate, in one place. The vocabulary that makes team friction discussable.

tools.name: Core Domain Charts
tools.note: For arguing about where to spend your best people, with a picture instead of opinions.

tools.name: Domain Message Flow Modelling
tools.note: Shows how a single scenario crosses your context boundaries, which is where designs usually turn out to be wrong.

tools.name: Context Mapping quiz
tools.note: Interactive, and a faster way to find out you have misunderstood a pattern than reading about it again.

tools.name: Strategic architecture building blocks
tools.note: An earlier exploration, kept for reference. Say so when linking it: it is an archived direction, not current advice.

tools.name: Bounded Context Canvas
tools.note: The most used canvas in the set. Fills the gap between naming a context and knowing what it is responsible for.

tools.name: Aggregate Design Canvas
tools.note: For when the vocabulary starts to bite and someone asks what an aggregate actually is in your system.

tools.name: CoMo Prep Canvas
tools.note: Preparation for a collaborative modelling session, which is the part people skip and then blame the workshop.

tools.name: Debiasing decisions toolkit
tools.note: Structured interventions for better group decisions. Closest of all of these to what this community is actually about.

tools.name: EventStorming Glossary Cheat Sheet
tools.note: One page that settles what the sticky colours mean, which is most of the confusion in a first EventStorming.

tools.name: Virtual Modelling Templates
tools.note: Ready-made boards, so a remote session does not start with half an hour of drawing rectangles.
